log: Act V in one piece, from the frozen end of Act IV (she stands free in the house): the climb, the high valley, the Anlage with the trial and the load, the letting go, the Grat with the cleft, the child, the first house, and the way down to the house, where the act ends quietly. Nothing is set up: every flag, facet and stage comes from the play (the keeper is let go at the console, so he comes to the hearth at the end)
the end of Act IV: the house
out into the valley
the west path leads onto the road
the third arrow in chalk, next to the signpost with two
the door at the north rim of the meadow: into the mountains
the walk up begins on the path
the first cairn: the next stands where this one can be seen
a strip of net on a post: the first answer at the gate was the boundary
two planks over the brook
the sign: summit, soon
the iron ring in the rock: a trace of the world
the look-out: the smoke of the Anlage
the slate chip: taken with the first answer
the scree is gone from the end of the path: a door into the high valley
the walk goes one step on
the sign: view, and the arrow points at a wall
the little round stone at the foot of the first cairn: taken with the first answer
the stone's quest begins with the stone
the first cairn: the stone laid on top rolls off
the print of a hand on the flat stone at the tarn: the first flashback
the second cairn: the stone tips over
the third cairn: the wind takes it, and in the end it is in her pocket
the stone's quest ends with the third try
the marmot's hoard on the slope: the thimble on top
the crystal in the scree at the north shore
the gate of the Anlage: the first answer is to knock, and the gate opens with the last line
the door in the open gate: the hall
the walk: the Anlage
the keeper counts her and offers the trial: the first answer is to see the levers
lever one first: the wrong order, one line, and the three go back
lever three
lever one
lever two: three, one, two as he called it
a lever under a cloth: it stands
the bolt of the small door, seen and not talked about
the dials: all on normal, one trembles
the dial with the groove in its glass: a trace of the world
the pipe that hisses in time with the ticking at the gate
after the trial: the first answer is the offer, begin the load
she stands at the console and pulls nothing: the levers spring up, the load shows; each wave calls its levers
the fourth wave has run its time: he reckons it up and keeps to it
after the load: he counts the open levers and keeps a reservation
the load has stopped and every lever stands up: she steps away from the console and waits; nothing is asked of her
the levers go down by themselves, something goes wrong, a lamp goes out
the last lever is down: the bar of clicks
the hall has settled: he enters it all and doubts it
the walk goes one step on
a potato lies by the pipe on the left: she takes it
after the letting go: he checks it, counts, and keeps to the procedure
the door back into the high valley
the foot of the ramp: blocker and scree are gone
the top of the ramp: the Grat; the walk goes on
the first look from the Grat
the signpost at the fork round the rock island: two arrows in charcoal
the mouth of the cleft
the end of the cleft: the narrow way taken to its end, the hollow in the rock, the second flashback
the candle stub in the hollow: the first answer takes it
the plateau's edge: a free place, wind
the child sits on the flat stone at the edge of the plateau, looking down into the valley: she talks to it before she sits, and gets only narration (the child does not look up)
the stone beside the child
she sits down beside it: the child hums, six frames hang in the air, the answer, the child is gone
the walk goes one step on
in the valley a shoot grows in the bed
on the plateau a small house stands where nothing was
the look at the south edge now tells about the house
the house from the front (beside its door, which would take her in)
the book on its post: leafing through it, the last page is empty
a trace of the world
through the low door into the one room
the walk goes one step on
the first look: the window, the lines, the bed
the outermost ring, along the walls
the innermost, round the bed
the window is chalked over (without the facet only the look is offered)
a stick of blue chalk on the floor: she takes it
at the bed: the third picture, a room and a bed and an open window
the picture is held: the sixth frame will show it
the door back onto the plateau
and down again: the door back to the pass
the way down, seen from the other side
the foot of the pass
the valley: the walk is home
she came down without the house on the plateau: nothing is a condition
the bed: one shoot between the weeds
home
the homecoming (without the facet: a quiet house and an empty hearth) and the end of the act
the mark of the chapter, quietly
Act V is over: the walk is done, the chapter marked, she stands in the house
